sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page farn1234 and Glottolog 5.1 sources.bib (local copy) entries matching nsf / Yangbi / Yunlong / Yongping
sources.note: Bibliography only: Yang 2018 (phonology), Li 1996 (grammar_sketch), Zhu 2005 (overview), Yang 2009, ISO CR 2011-007. No other descriptive work on nsf in Glottolog.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Nisu language' (en) and '彝语南部方言' (zh), accessed 2026-09-17
sources.note: Nothing on stress; phonology sections are unsourced and describe Xinping (Northern Nisu). Identity only: FNW Nisu = Beidou Township, Yongping (citing Blackburn & Blackburn 2007); zh: 西北尼苏语, 24,000 speakers in 漾濞, 云龙, 永平.

sources.citation: Lama, Ziwo Qiu-Fuyuan. 2012. Subgrouping of Nisoic (Yi) Languages: A Study from the Perspectives of Shared Innovation and Phylogenetic Estimation. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Arlington. 399 pp. hdl 10106/11161.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: online with a Harvard login (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Silent: 'stress'/'accent' occur nowhere in the text. Nisu profile (pp. 77-78) covers Jiangcheng Nisu and Xinping Nishu only (three tones 55/33/21); no Dali/Yongping/Yangbi/Yunlong variety in the study. Not FNW Nisu.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2011. Change Request 2011-007 (submitted by Eric Johnson, SIL East Asia Group): create [nsf] Nisu, Far Northwestern; adopted 2012-02-03. 5 + 3 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Identity: Fuheng district of Yangbi, Tuanjie Yi district of Yunlong, Beidou Yi district of Yongping (Dali Bai Autonomous Prefecture), ca. 24,000 speakers (2004); evidence = Blackburn & Blackburn 2007 400-item wordlist and Cathryn Yang 2008 1,000-item wordlist (both unpublished), Yang 2009.

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2009. Nisu Dialect Geography. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2009-007. 35 pp. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.note: Silent: the words stress/accent do not occur. Sec. 1.3 (pp. 4-6) gives a pan-Nisu inventory from Xinping Laochang (tonemes High 55 / Mid 33 / Low 21, tense/lax vowels). FNW Nisu appears only as datapoint 'YP BD Far NW Yongping Beidou (Blackburn and Blackburn 2007)' (App. 1, p. 31) and in p. 3 ('located to the far northwest of other Nisu varieties... beyond the scope of this research') and sec. 4.3.1 ('Yongping (YP) Nisu is found to be very different from all other Nisu varieties').

sources.citation: Li, Shengfu 李生福. 1996. 彝语南部方言研究 [Research on the Southern dialect of Yi]. Beijing: Minzu chubanshe. 4+292 pp.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Glottolog's grammar_sketch for nsf, but its NW datapoint is Shuangbai (E-Xin = Northern Nisu [yiv]) per Yang 2009; its stress passage (p. ~14, per sister-folder snippets) is a pan-Yi statement on 表意重音/表情重音 with Shuangbai examples. Would document Nisu-cluster stress, not specifically FNW.

sources.citation: Yang, Wenjing 杨文静. 2018. 大理州彝语佬倵话语音研究 [A phonetic study of the Laowu (Nisu) dialect of Yi in Dali Prefecture]. MA thesis, Yunnan Normal University. 108 pp.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; Harvard e-access not checked
sources.note: The only phonology of this exact language (Tuanjie township, Yunlong; speakers self-name Nisu = nsf). Chinese MA phonologies of Yi varieties normally have sections on 音节结构, 声调 and 语流音变 where any 重音 (stress) statement would sit.

sources.citation: Chen, Kang 陈康. 2010. 彝语方言研究 [A study of Yi dialects]. Beijing: Zhongyang Minzu Daxue Chubanshe. 634 pp.

sources.note: Largest modern comparative description of Yi dialects with per-datapoint phonologies; may include a Dali-area Nisu (Yangbi/Yunlong) datapoint and a section on 重音; not verified from here.

sources.citation: Blackburn, P. L. & Laura Blackburn. 2007. Yongping Nisu wordlist. Dali: SIL East Asia Group (ms.).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only published-cited primary data on Beidou/Yongping FNW Nisu (400 items, used by Yang 2009 and the ISO change request); a transcribed wordlist may mark prominence but is unpublished.

sources.citation: Zhu, Wenxu 朱文旭. 2005. 彝语方言学 [Yi dialectology]. Beijing: Zhongyang Minzu Daxue Chubanshe. 430 pp. ISBN 9787810569842.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Comparative overview with ten datapoints, one of which is Yangbi (= FNW Nisu per Glottolog); contains a Yangbi sound-system sketch and a general 声调/重音 passage ('有的音节还有表意重音或表情重音'), which may be the closest thing in print to a stress statement for this variety.
